title: verdict
description: The grader's output, produced under constrained decoding. Field order within a dimension is load-bearing: evidence, then reasoning, then score. The model emits fields in schema order, so this forces it to quote the candidate and argue before committing to a number. Score-first would let it pick a number and rationalise afterwards, which is a different and worse task. `recommendation` is deliberately absent: it is a pure function of `overall`, and asking the model for it produced strong_yes on candidates scored 2 of 5 in two runs. Constrained decoding guarantees shape, not coherence between fields - every enum value satisfies the schema. It is derived in code.

evidence.description: Quote or closely paraphrase what the candidate actually said. Write this before deciding a score.

reasoning.description: How that evidence maps to the rubric.

score.description: Integer from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Must follow from the evidence above.
